chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who visited the House (performed Umrah) before shaving [his head]. He said, 'It is not appropriate except that he be forgetful.'
Then he said, 'The people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Sacrifice, and some of them said,
And that which indicates what we mentioned regarding the repetition of Tawaf and Sa'i is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْبَيْتَ: The House (Kaaba), referring to performing Umrah
key_terms.لاَ حَرَجَ: No blame/penalty (a legal term for leniency in minor errors)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before stoning the Jamarat?
ai.summary: In the context of Hajj jurisprudence, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that performing the final shaving (Halq) before stoning the Jamarat is a minor error (khata) excusable by forgetfulness, rather than a major breach requiring re-performance. The Imam grounds this ruling in the Prophet’s precedent of 'La haraj' (no hardship) for the Companions' varied order-of-operations mistakes, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease and the non-cumulative nature of these specific pillars. This highlights the distinction between essential pillars (arkan) and obligatory acts (wajibat) in Usul al-Fiqh.
